items.title: Pregnancy check-ups should be carried out as planned
items.core: Regular prenatal check-ups can detect problems early.
body: Record the results of each inspection.
Concentrate your questions on the doctor.
Write the gestational age, appointment time and required documents into the calendar, and confirm the hospital department and fasting requirements three days before the prenatal check-up.
Bring all previous laboratory test sheets and ultrasound sheets with you every time, and ask the doctor whether the screening results are abnormal and the next step according to the gestational age.
If you experience abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, headache, dizziness, or significant decrease in fetal movement, seek medical attention immediately without waiting for an appointment.

Case: When she was 24 weeks pregnant, Ms. Lin went to the hospital for a glucose tolerance test as scheduled and found that her blood sugar was high. She then adjusted her diet and exercise under the guidance of a doctor. After the reexamination, she controlled it within the target range. She also continued to follow up on follow-up prenatal check-ups.

items.title: Baby sleep safety is priority
items.core: Sleep environment is more important than sleeping position products.
body: Sleep on your back, use a hard mattress, and have few items on the bed.
Avoid overheating and cover mouth and nose.
The baby sleeps alone on a solid, flat mattress, leaving only the baby and a tightly wrapped sleeping bag on the bed.
Do not put pillows, stuffed toys, thick quilts and bed guards on the bed to prevent your mouth and nose from being blocked or entangled.
Stay in the same room with your parents and use different beds for at least six months. The room temperature should be warm and the back of the baby's neck is warm and free of sweat.

Case: When the baby was three months old, the parents removed the stuffed toys and thick quilts from the crib, let the baby sleep on his back on a flat mattress, and used a sleeping bag to keep warm at night. After that, he slept more peacefully throughout the night and did not cover his mouth and nose.

items.title: Feeding follows signals
items.core: Feeding on demand does not mean feeding at any time.
body: Recognize hunger and satiety signals.
Record the growth curve.
First observe early signs such as turning head to look for breasts, sucking hands, smacking lips, etc. Crying is usually a later sign.
Record the start time, length of one side and number of diapers each time. If the interval is often shorter than one hour, investigate the cause.
Slowing down in feeding, taking the initiative to let go, and having a satisfied expression are considered full; if the weight gain is less than 600 grams during the full month, please consult.

Case: When the baby was two months old, the mother originally planned to feed her baby every two hours. Later, she recorded her feeding and sleep. She found that when he was hungry, he would turn his head to look for milk and suck his hands. When he was full, he would actively let go. After feeding according to the signal, he would vomit less milk and gain normal weight.

items.title: Vaccine vaccination on time
items.core: After a missed vaccination, follow the catch-up rules.
body: Keep vaccination records.
Watch for reactions after vaccination.
After creating the card, take photos and archives of the age and dose of each vaccine, and check whether the interval is reached before making an appointment.
If you miss a vaccination, do not re-vaccinate yourself. Bring your vaccination certificate to the clinic for re-vaccination according to the minimum interval and unfinished doses.
Consult your doctor first if you have fever, acute diarrhea, or are taking immunosuppressive drugs, and make arrangements after you recover.

Case: The child missed the second dose of DPT due to fever. The mother brought the vaccination certificate to the community outpatient clinic for consultation, and made a new appointment according to the re-vaccination interval given by the doctor. After completion, the vaccination record was checked to be complete. There was no repeated replenishment of materials due to missed vaccinations when entering the nursery.

items.title: Add complementary foods step by step
items.core: Add only one new food at a time.
body: Watch for allergic reactions.
Less salt and less sugar.
Choose iron-fortified rice flour or puree for the first time, and try only a small amount during the day for two or three days in a row.
Place new foods in the morning or noon and observe rash, vomiting, diarrhea and coughing before deciding whether to continue.
From a slimy paste to small particles, don’t use soup rice as a substitute for a meal, encourage yourself to hold a spoon and chew.

Case: On the first day when the baby turned six months old, grandma only gave him a small spoonful of iron-fortified rice noodles. After observing for two days that there was no rash or diarrhea, she added pumpkin puree. If she felt any discomfort, she could immediately identify which new food it was.

items.title: Response is more important than device
items.core: Soothing comes from human interaction.
body: Respond to cries and expressions promptly.
Don’t rely on electronic devices.
When the baby cries, first squat down and look straight up, confirm the needs with a low voice and short sentences, and then check the diaper, hunger, cold and heat.
Put down your phone and imitate face-to-face expressions and respond with sounds. Just fix it for a few minutes a few times a day.
Before using a napkin or rocking chair, check to see if the baby wants to interact. If the baby is staring at someone, respond first.

Case: When the baby cried at night, the father did not immediately turn on the animation to comfort him. Instead, he picked him up, talked softly, patted his back and fed him. The baby fell back to sleep ten minutes later and was more willing to look at and interact with his parents during the next day.

items.title: Parent-child reading starts from a few minutes
items.core: Fixed time is more important than duration.
body: Read a short paragraph every day.
Let the child turn the pages.
Tie reading to the same sequence before going to bed, brushing teeth or after taking a bath, and it will be easier for children to get into the mood.
Only one small book is taught at a time, and the children will follow the pages as they turn, without rushing to correct the plot or finish reading.
Choose books with clear physical pictures and short sentences, name the pictures and wait for the child to speak for three seconds before continuing.

Case: Mom puts the picture book on the bedside and reads it for three minutes every day after taking a bath, even if she only reads one page. After two weeks, the baby will take the initiative to sit on the bedside with the book, and the crying before going to bed is significantly reduced.

items.title: Use safety seats in cars
items.core: It is not safe to hold in your arms.
body: Select by age and weight.
Use every time.
Select the seat group according to the child's weight and height. After installation, the left and right swing should not exceed 2.5 cm.
Install rear-facing until the height and weight limit specified by the seat is reached. Do not turn in advance just based on age.
The child sits in the back seat, the safety belt is belted according to the instruction manual, and the five-point buckle is tightened so that only one finger can be inserted.

Case: A family of three drove by themselves on the weekend. The grandmother originally wanted to sit in the back seat with her one-year-old baby in her arms, but the parents insisted on installing a safety seat and checking the buckles. The baby was firmly secured when the car suddenly braked on the way, and the whole family was not injured.

items.title: Prevent falls at home
items.core: Protect cribs and stairs.
body: Fixed cabinets, doors and windows.
Keep the floor clean and tidy.
The gap between the bed rails should not exceed six centimeters, the mattress should be adjusted to the lowest setting, and there should be no climbable boxes next to the bed.
Install a solid safety door at the entrance of the stairs and do not open it in the direction of the stairs to prevent children from rolling down after being pushed open.
Beds and sofas should be kept away from windows, and limiters should be installed. If the gap between railings is too large, use transparent protective panels.

Case: After the baby was able to turn over, the father adjusted the crib mattress to the lowest position, installed a safety door at the stairwell, and laid a non-slip mat next to the sofa. When the child was learning to crawl, it was blocked several times when he came close to the edge and did not fall.

items.title: Prevent swallowing small objects
items.core: Keep coins and button batteries away.
body: Inspect the ground from a child's perspective.
The medicines are locked.
Use a one-yuan coin to test the gaps between the floor drain and the table. Any gaps that can fit a coin need to be sealed or replaced.
Place button battery remote controls, electronic scales and luminous toys in high places, and screw back the battery covers immediately after use.
Lidded boxes for pills, candies and nuts, not on the bedside or on the desktop within easy reach.

Case: Grandpa put the button battery on the coffee table, and the two-year-old child picked it up and wanted to put it in his mouth. The mother took it away immediately after noticing it, and put the change and battery into the upper drawer. The child did not touch small objects again after that.

items.title: Establish a sleep routine
items.core: A fixed routine to help you fall asleep.
body: Take a bath, tell a story, turn off the lights.
The order remains consistent.
Turn off the screen thirty minutes before going to bed, and proceed in the order of taking a bath, changing clothes, brushing teeth, and turning off the lights.
Use the same closing sentence and the same nightlight brightness every night to reduce the number of renegotiations and bedtimes.
When you wake up in the middle of the night, wait for a minute or two before checking with the lowest brightness. Avoid turning on the light or picking it up to play with immediately.

Case: At eight o'clock every night, the mother first bathes the baby, then turns off the lights, changes the sleeping bag, and sings the same lullaby. At first, the baby will roll over and play, but after a week, the baby will quietly close his eyes when hearing the lullaby, and the time to fall asleep is shortened.

items.title: Night care requires division of labor
items.core: Staying up late alone is not sustainable for a long time.
body: Arrange the rotation in advance.
Compensatory rest during the day.
Alternate night shifts on weekdays and weekends, and write down feeding, diaper changing and soothing responsibilities in advance.
When the night feeding is divided, the person who is not feeding is responsible for recording, burping, or getting up early the next day to make up for the shift.
If you sleep less than five hours for three consecutive nights, you will be rescheduled. If necessary, ask a family member to provide you with a full night of sleep.

Case: When the baby wakes up continuously at night, the couple agrees that the mother will breastfeed and the father will change diapers and comfort them on weekdays. In the middle of the night before the exchange on weekends, they can each sleep for four hours continuously. After a month of persistence, they will be more patient in taking care of the child during the day.

items.title: Record growth changes
items.core: Data is more reliable than impressions.
body: Measure height and weight regularly.
Keep the physical examination report.
Measure height and weight at the same time every month, on an empty stomach in the morning or two hours after a meal.
Write the numerical value, measurement date and physical changes into the table to avoid judging based on "it seems to have grown taller".
Record continuously for three to six months. If the curve flattens or fluctuates significantly, bring the watch and seek medical consultation.

Case: The mother measured her child's height and weight every month and recorded it in the same form. Half a year later, she found that the growth rate had slowed down. She brought the data to see a doctor, and the doctor promptly adjusted her dietary recommendations.

items.title: Don’t delay your medical checkup appointment
items.core: Schedule your checkup according to your age.
body: 列出时间表。
记录异常指标。
List the annual physical examination items by age and gender, and write the appointment on the calendar in your birthday month.
Increase special screening for people with family medical history, and proactively inform the doctor of relevant medical history when making an appointment.
After the physical examination, save the report and list of abnormal items, and set reminders for re-examination as recommended by the doctor.

Case: Dad’s physical examination was postponed for two years. The physical examination at work found thyroid nodules and high blood pressure. He made an appointment for a reexamination on the same day and finally dealt with it early without affecting his work.

items.title: Be careful when using medication in children
items.core: Dosage is calculated based on body weight.
body: Do not use adult drugs on your own.
Keep drug instructions.
Before taking the medicine, read the children's weight dosage table in the instructions. If you do not follow the adult dosage, simply halve it.
Use the matching measuring cup or syringe to take the medicine, record the medicine name, time, and dose to avoid repeated dosing.
Before taking two or more medicines at the same time, ask your doctor or pharmacist to confirm whether the ingredients are duplicated.

Case: The child had a fever, and the grandmother took half a tablet of antipyretic medicine based on adult experience. After the mother found out, she checked the dosage according to her weight and consulted a pharmacist to avoid overdose and her body temperature was safely controlled.

items.title: Learn to take your temperature
items.core: The data is the basis for medical treatment.
body: Choose the right thermometer.
Record time and value.
Choose a thermometer suitable for your age. The armpit temperature should be clamped for five minutes, and the ear temperature should be measured at the correct angle.
Record every four to six hours when you have a fever, and also write down the time of taking medicine and changes in body temperature.
When seeking medical treatment, directly report the highest body temperature, duration and accompanying symptoms. Don’t just say “very hot”.

Case: The child had a fever at night. The father used an ear thermometer to measure the temperature three times in a row and recorded the time and value. He showed it to the doctor when he saw the doctor the next day. The doctor quickly judged that there was no need to blindly use antibiotics.

items.title: Prepare a list of questions before seeing a doctor
items.core: The clinic time is short and it is easy to miss.
body: Write down symptoms and a timeline.
带上既往记录。
Write down the main symptoms, time of occurrence, aggravating factors and tried treatments before seeking medical treatment.
Take photos with you of the name, dosage and allergy history of the medicine you are taking to avoid the doctor prescribing medicines repeatedly.
Order the three most worrying questions in order of importance, and ask the most critical questions first during the outpatient visit.

Case: Before taking the old man to the clinic, my mother wrote down the time when the symptoms started, the medication, and three questions. During the diagnosis and treatment, she asked questions one by one. The doctor adjusted the dosage of the medicine, reducing repeated visits to the hospital.

items.title: The status of the caregiver is also important
items.core: Take care of yourself first when taking care of others.
body: Arrange for replacement staff.
Don’t be proud of being tired.
Set aside at least fifteen minutes of alone time every day to drink water, stretch or close your eyes to rest. Don’t push yourself.
List the tasks of turning over, feeding, and accompanying patients, and ask family members to claim one or two of them regularly.
If you have persistent insomnia, irritability or body pain, seek help from relatives, friends or a doctor in time.

Case: The wife took care of her husband who had suffered a stroke for three months. She turned over every night, and she began to suffer from insomnia and panic. After asking a relative to take a half-day break, the care became more patient, and the husband's recovery became more stable.

items.title: The reading habit starts with a few minutes a day
items.core: A fixed time is more important than intensity.
body: Keep books at your fingertips.
Don’t turn reading into an assessment.
Fix a triggering scene, such as after dinner or before going to bed, and read for five minutes before deciding whether to continue.
Put the book on the sofa, bedside or in your bag, making it more convenient to pick up the book than open the short video.
Write a sentence about your feelings after each chapter, read it again after a week, and use very small feedback to maintain continuity.

Case: An office worker switched from browsing his mobile phone to reading a five-page book before going to bed. At first, he only persisted for five minutes. After two months, he developed a habit and took the initiative to bring a book with him when commuting.

items.title: Guaranteed outdoor activities
items.core: Vision and mood benefit.
body: Set aside some time outside each day.
Events don’t have to be expensive.
Arrange twenty to thirty minutes of outdoor activities every day, giving priority to venues with natural light.
Bind outdoor time with fixed tasks, such as going downstairs after school and then going home to do homework.
Arrange a family hike, ball game or bike ride on the weekend to let your children make outdoor activities their daily routine.

Case: A primary school student rides a bicycle in the community for twenty minutes after school every day and goes for a walk in the park on weekends. After three months, his myopia has not increased significantly and he can fall asleep more smoothly at night.

items.title: Have boundaries around screen time
items.core: Clear rules are more effective than ad hoc scrambling.
body: Agree on duration and content.
Adults also comply.
Work with your children to write down the time, duration and viewing content of the screen each day, and post it.
Use the timer to remind you five minutes in advance, and calmly withdraw it after the time is up, without temporarily adding reward time.
Parents themselves should abide by the dining table and not look at their mobile phones, so that the rules will not easily become unilateral requirements.

Case: Parents and children agreed that they could watch animations for twenty minutes after finishing their homework, and the timer would automatically pause when the timer expired. The children complained at first, but were able to return the tablets themselves after a few days.

items.title: The rules must be consistent
items.core: Inconsistency can cause children to test boundaries.
body: Family members share the same message.
The consequences of a violation must be predictable.
Write family rules into a short list, and use the same rules for eating, sleeping, screen and other scenes.
When caregivers temporarily want to relax the rules, communicate privately first and do not undermine each other in front of the children.
If you violate the rules, you will be dealt with according to the pre-agreement, keep your tone stable, and avoid being punished today and forget it tomorrow.

Case: The child discovered that his mother did not allow him to eat snacks before meals, but his grandma secretly gave him biscuits, so he started quarreling before meals every day. After the whole family held a meeting to unify the snack time, the disputes were significantly reduced.

items.title: Don’t compare your children to others
items.core: Comparisons harm relationships rather than inspire.
body: Describe specific behaviors rather than evaluating people.
Focus on his own progress.
Only describe the child's own progress when evaluating, such as "wrong three fewer questions than last time" rather than "others are better".
When you want to motivate, first ask where the difficulty is, and then break it down into achievable small goals together.
Avoid commenting on your child’s shortcomings in front of relatives and friends. Protecting self-esteem is more important than winning face on the spot.

Case: Parents often compared the perfect scores of their neighbor's children, and the son became more and more silent. Later, he only compared it with his own last score, pointed out mistakes and improved them, and the child took the initiative to share his study plan.

items.title: Play is a child’s job
items.core: Free play promotes development.
body: Leave unstructured time.
Do not have a full schedule.
Set aside at least thirty minutes of free play time every day without any assignments, and let your children decide on their own content.
Provide open materials such as building blocks, cartons, and fabrics, and use fewer toys that only have one way to play.
Adults should interrupt and correct less. When a child asks for help, use questions to guide him to continue trying.

Case: Over the weekend, parents changed the pinyin class to free building blocks. The children used the building blocks to build small stations, and also took the initiative to explain the routes and ticketing rules. Their expression and planning abilities were improved.

items.title: Respond seriously to questions
items.core: Curiosity needs to be caught.
body: If you don’t know, check it out together.
Don’t be perfunctory or over-explain.
When your child asks a question, stop what you are doing, squat down and look at him and say, ‘This is a great question’, to make him feel valued.
If you don’t know the answer, don’t make it up. You can agree to check a book or search together and tell him the process of finding it.
After answering, add a rhetorical question, such as ‘What do you think?’, turning the question into continuous observation and discussion.

Case: After dinner, the child asked "Why does the moon follow the car?" The father did not hesitate. He stopped the car and took him to observe the shadows of trees on the roadside. When he went home, he looked up pictures to explain relative motion. The child drew diagrams and continued to ask about the stars.

items.title: Have rules for screen time
items.core: Clear boundaries are better than ad hoc scrambling.
body: Agree on duration and content.
Adults also comply.
Agree with your children in advance on the available time, usage periods and ending actions each day, and write it down as a chart and post it in the living room.
Use a timer or alarm clock to remind you five minutes in advance, and only execute it once: ‘Turn off the phone now and go to the next arrangement’.
Put the screen in a public area and charge the devices together before going to bed to avoid temporary competition and secret extension.

Case: On weekend mornings, the child wanted to watch the tablet continuously. The mother took out the timer agreed in advance and explained that after watching an episode, she needed to collect the toys before riding outdoors. Although the child complained, she finally followed the rules.

items.title: Involve children in housework
items.core: Participation brings a sense of responsibility.
body: Start with simple tasks.
Do not pursue perfect results.
Assign fixed chores according to age, such as collecting toys for three-year-olds and setting out dishes for six-year-olds. The tasks should be simple and sustainable.
Use graphic step cards to indicate ‘what to do first and what to do’ to reduce urging and allow children to complete it independently.
Concrete feedback after completion, such as ‘I picked up all the hair on the floor’, don’t just give a general ‘awesome’.

Case: After breakfast on Saturday, the mother asked the child to sort the dirty clothes into the basket and wipe the table. He matched the socks and wiped the table. During the meal, he took the initiative to say that he was also a little helper at home.

items.title: Give limited choices
items.core: The power of choice reduces confrontation.
body: Provide two or three options.
The results are acceptable.
Set the acceptable range first, and then give two to three options, such as ‘brush your teeth first or wash your face first’.
The wording of the options should be neutral and do not say ‘Are you willing to do it obediently’ to prevent children from grabbing negative words to fight.
Enter the next step immediately after the child makes a choice, without repeated persuasion or additional conditions, making the choice truly effective.

Case: The child refused to wear a coat in the morning. The mother took out two red and blue coats and asked "Which one to wear?" and asked him to choose zippers or buttons. The child chose the blue coat and put it on before going out without any further stalemate.

items.title: Let natural consequences speak for themselves
items.core: Experience results within the confines of safety.
body: Don’t bear all the consequences for your children.
Review together afterwards.
First determine whether the consequences are safe and controllable. When injuries or major losses are involved, children must still be protected directly.
Just remind once, and replace repeated warnings with specific results such as 'you will get your clothes wet and you need to change them yourself'.
Don’t laugh or scold him afterwards, guide him to tell you how to do it next time, and turn the experience into executable experience.

Case: The child refused to bring an umbrella before it started to rain. The mother only reminded her once and respected the decision. After getting wet after school, the children changed their clothes and wiped their schoolbags by themselves, and took the initiative to stuff their umbrellas into the side pockets of their schoolbags before going out the next day.

items.title: Praise the process, not the talent
items.core: Hard work is more controllable than cleverness.
body: Tell me how to do it.
Avoid labels.
Describe specific actions, such as 'You just changed three methods' to let the child know which step is worth repeating.
Use less words like ‘genius, cleverness, and natural ability’ and more words like ‘focus, persistence, inspection, and improvement’.
After praising, ask ‘which step is the most useful’ to help the child review the method instead of just seeking to be praised.

Case: The child failed the puzzle many times and wanted to give up. Instead of saying "You are so smart", the father pointed out that he had been spinning and trying the corners and encouraged him to try another method. Finally, the child completed the puzzle and said "I will keep looking".

items.title: No personality labels
items.core: Labels can become self-prophetic.
body: Describe behaviors rather than define people.
Point out the parts that can be changed.
Change the evaluation from personality to behavior, and replace 'Why are you so selfish' with 'You just cut in line'.
Describe the specific actions expected, such as ‘Wheel on the ground, don’t press other people’s feet’, and children will be more likely to follow it.
After inevitable mistakes, say ‘How can I make up for it this time?’ to prevent children from taking mistakes as their identity.

Case: The child was running around in the supermarket. Instead of scolding him, "You are so naughty," the mother pulled him to her side and said, "Go slowly between the shelves," and asked him to help get yogurt. The child then quietly completed the purchase while holding the shopping cart.

items.title: Help children name their emotions
items.core: If you can talk, you can handle it.
body: Use specific emotion words.
Don’t be in a hurry to reason.
First observe expressions and events, then guess the emotions using ‘Are you a little...’ and give your children vocabulary.
Allow the child to say no and respond with ‘Okay, let’s sit quietly for a while’ to ‘I’m not angry’.
Pause for a moment after naming, don’t rush to reason, wait for your breathing to stabilize before discussing what to do.

Case: After the building blocks collapsed, the child fell on the mat and cried. The mother knelt down and said, "You are very disappointed, you still want to build a higher building." The child nodded and said, "I am angry," and then agreed to build the bottom floor together.

items.title: Rules need to explain why
items.core: Understanding lasts longer than obedience.
body: Explain clearly what the rules protect.
Keep the caliber consistent.
Explain the interests protected by the rules, such as ‘Sitting in a safety chair prevents injuries from sudden braking’, which will make it easier for children to accept it.
Explanations should be short and close to the current scene, avoid long sermons, and give the next step immediately after speaking.
When the child refutes, listen to the reasons first, then add the key reasons, and let him participate in deciding the reminder method.

Case: The child wants to eat sweets before dinner. The mother asks him to look at pictures of dental plaque and a dental check-in chart. She explains that time should be left for cleaning the teeth after the sweets. The child takes the initiative to brush his teeth before eating after the meal.

items.title: The rules must be implemented consistently
items.core: Inconsistency will make children tempted.
body: Family members have unified standards.
The consequences are predictable.
Caregivers first unify the list of rules, including times, steps and exceptions, to avoid one person being relaxed and the other being strict.
Exceptions should state the boundaries and times in advance, such as ‘Ten minutes more tonight, only on birthdays’.
The words should be short and steady during execution, and the rules should not be increased due to crying, nor should the rules be temporarily canceled due to good performance.

Case: The family agreed to turn off the lights at nine o'clock. On Monday, the mother relented and extended the time. On Tuesday, the father urged her in advance, and the child cried and tried. Later, the two unified the process and vocabulary. Three days later, the child collected his toys and washed himself when he arrived.

items.title: Maintain communication with teachers
items.core: Home and school information need to be aligned.
body: Understand classroom performance.
Don’t deny the teacher in front of the children.
Spend one or two minutes each week to exchange information, focusing on asking about work and rest, peers, and study status.
A brief explanation when giving feedback on family changes, such as moving, having a second child, or getting sick, helps the teacher understand recent performance.
When encountering a problem, first verify the details and then discuss solutions together. Do not unilaterally blame the teacher in front of the children.

Case: The child refused to take a nap for several days in a row. The mother asked the teacher during pick-up and drop-off and learned that the sleeping room location had been changed. When she got home, she explained the procedure in advance and brought a small pillow cover. The child took a nap peacefully the next day and his mood improved.

items.title: Focus on peer relationships
items.core: Friend relationships affect emotions.
body: Understand the situation of getting along.
Prompt support when being excluded.
Use open questions to chat with your peers every day, such as ‘Who did you have the most fun with today?’ Don’t just ask about grades and homework.
When you hear someone being excluded, comfort them first and ask for details, distinguishing between occasional conflicts, misunderstandings and continued isolation.
Create opportunities through playdates, role exercises and class activities, and ask teachers to assist in observation when necessary.

Case: After school, the child said that no one played with him. The father did not deny it. He asked for three consecutive days who refused and where to play, and invited classmates to come home to build building blocks. The child gradually had a regular playmate.

items.title: The division of housework must be visible
items.core: Invisible labor is most easily ignored.
body: Make a list and frequency.
Redistribute periodically.
Use a shared list to mark who and when tasks such as laundry and taking out the trash are completed one by one, so as not to just remember them in your head.
Take a photo of a clean kitchen or tidy room every Sunday night to visually see the results and consumption of your work.
Indicate the frequency of invisible activities such as purchasing toilet paper and seasonal storage, and rotate the person in charge and the acceptance person every month.

Case: The wife silently does housework every day, but the husband always turns a blind eye. Once, the wife made a list of housework and posted it on the refrigerator. After doing it for a day, the husband started to complain from exhaustion and realized how hard his wife had worked.

items.title: Allow time for couples to communicate
items.core: Don’t discuss things when you are tired.
body: Fix a period of time that will not be interrupted.
Let’s talk about facts first and then feelings.
It is agreed that 20:30 every Wednesday will be an exclusive chat window. The mobile phone will be placed in the living room and the duration is limited to 40 minutes.
When the dispute escalates, first say that you need to rest for twenty minutes, and then return to the table to continue after your heart rate stabilizes.

Use a fixed code such as a yellow cup to indicate that you want to talk about something on your mind. When the other party sees it, he will take the initiative to pause the game at hand or watch a TV show.

Case: Xiao Li and his wife often quarreled over trivial matters. Later, they agreed to chat for half an hour every day after the children went to bed. Once they talked about family planning, the two became calm and resolved the conflicts that had been accumulated for many days.

items.title: Consent in Intimate Relationships
items.core: Default is not a substitute for explicitness.
body: Important decisions are confirmed by both parties.
Respect the right to change your mind at any time.
Incorporate specific behaviors such as holding hands and hugging into the scope of inquiry, and use “can it” instead of silence or guessing?
Stop immediately when the other party says to stop, and confirm whether you need water or alone time, without asking for reasons or excuses.
Confirm with your eyes for three seconds before each intimacy. If you are drunk or tired, it will be considered unauthorized by default.

Case: Xiao Wang acquiesced that his wife was willing to accompany him to watch football games, but his wife wanted to go shopping. After the two expressed their thoughts frankly, they agreed to take turns arranging weekend activities, and each other's boundaries were respected.

items.title: There must be boundaries between generations
items.core: Care does not mean taking over.
body: Make it clear who gets to decide what.
Appreciate the help but don’t give up the initiative.
When parents intervene in child care, we should first say thank you for the advice, and then make it clear that we make the decision ourselves and bear the consequences.
If elders enter the room to tidy up without permission, they can put personal belongings into a locked box and be told to knock on the door before moving.
On major events such as buying a house or changing jobs, only the conclusion will be reported, and family group voting will not be allowed to avoid multiple people directing.

Case: The mother always decides the job choice for Xiao Zhou without authorization, and Xiao Zhou makes it clear that he is responsible. After his mother stopped interfering, Xiao Zhou worked according to his own wishes and felt more fulfilled.

items.title: Be transparent about your family budget
items.core: The more transparent you are about money, the less likely you will argue.
body: Make a list of fixed spending and savings goals.
Discuss large expenditures in advance.
Write the three figures of salary, mortgage, and food into the same table on the 1st of every month, and each party will keep a copy.
Set up a joint account to automatically transfer a fixed proportion, and manage the remaining income separately without requiring transaction-by-transaction reporting.
For any non-daily expenses exceeding 800 yuan, first explain the purpose at the dinner table before deciding whether to use your savings.

Case: Xiao Zhang and his wife often quarreled over spending money. Later, they kept accounts together and disclosed their income and expenses. A month later, the two knew exactly where the money was spent, and they never blushed about money again.

items.title: Make the division of household chores public
items.core: Invisible labor is most easily ignored.
body: Make a list and frequency.
Redistribute periodically.
Post a weekly work division list on the refrigerator. Write down grocery shopping, washing dishes, and mopping the floor on the form and sign to confirm.
Use sticky notes of different colors to represent what has been done and what is to be done. When guests come to visit, they can see who is working at a glance.
Hold a ten-minute short meeting at the end of each month to discuss which items are too frequent and adjust the vesting for the next month on the spot.

Case: Husbands and wives often have disputes over housework. They list grocery shopping, cooking and other tasks and publicly claim them, rotating them every week. After a while, both of them understood the division of labor, and there were fewer complaints at home.

items.title: Be transparent about finances
items.core: The more transparent you are about money, the less likely you will argue.
body: List fixed expenses.
Discuss large expenditures in advance.
Organize the salary card balances, financial principal and liabilities of both parties into shared documents and update them every quarter.
The joint account balance is pushed to the two people's mobile phones every week, and a text explaining the purpose of large transfers is sent in advance.
Set an annual financial review date to check insurance, deposit targets and overspending categories item by item before setting the next year's quota.

Case: There is a big income gap between Xiao Chen and her husband, and they always avoid talking about money. Buying a house requires joint financing. They spread all their savings and liabilities and successfully reached a consensus after transparent communication.

items.title: Making major decisions together
items.core: It is easy to complain when one party makes the decision.
body: Give each other time to express.
Record the final agreement.
Write down three alternatives for moving, choosing a school, etc., and cross out the unacceptable ones together before voting.
Decisions where the amount exceeds 20% of the monthly income or affects the place of residence must be approved by both parties before being implemented.
When one party makes the decision first, the other party has the right to request a 24-hour cooling-off period during which a fait accompli will not be established.

Case: The husband decided to move the family without authorization, and the wife was very angry. Later, the two sat down to list the pros and cons of moving, and after weighing the pros and cons together, they made a new decision, and the wife's complaints disappeared.

items.title: Keep private time
items.core: Intimacy does not mean no space.
body: Agree on a time to be alone.
No response is required at any time.
Mark time on your calendar for alone time, such as a Tuesday night run or a Saturday morning reading, that won't be occupied temporarily.
When one party wears headphones, it is regarded as a do not disturb signal, unless it involves picking up a child or an emergency.
Allow one day each month for completely independent arrangements. There is no sharing of positioning and no need to report specific consumption details.

Case: Xiao Wang and his wife were inseparable, and his wife felt suffocated. Later, they agreed to spend half a day each week alone, with his wife studying illustration and Xiao Wang playing ball. Instead, they cherished their time together even more.

items.title: Family groups maintain boundaries
items.core: It is not necessary to respond to every message.
body: Set viewing period.
Don’t let group messages interrupt business.
Set the family group to Do Not Disturb but keep it on top. Browse it once a day after dinner without having to reply immediately.
Reply all health links and forwarded videos with a like emoticon, eliminating the need for explanations or arguments one by one.
For questions involving privacy, such as salary or pregnancy preparation, use private chat instead of discussing details in a large group.

Case: Xiao Zhou was bombarded with messages from family groups, especially relatives who always asked about privacy. He set up Do Not Disturb and only selected important messages to reply to. His relatives gradually got used to it, and Xiao Zhou became less annoyed.

items.title: The division of labor during festivals is decided in advance
items.core: Temporary arrangements are the easiest to dispute.
body: List preparations.
Make it clear who is responsible for what.
Pull up a shared list two weeks before the festival, claim tickets, prepare meals, and give gifts respectively and write down the deadlines.
Use drawing lots to decide who will be responsible for cleaning and who will be responsible for picking up relatives. The rules should be agreed in advance and not reneged on the spot.
Write the budget and purchasing website into the memo to avoid wasting time on repeated purchases or temporary price bargaining.

Case: During the Spring Festival last year, Xiao Li’s family had a quarrel over who was temporarily deciding who would cook. This year, they discussed the division of labor two weeks in advance and made a shopping and cooking list. The festival was harmonious and relaxed.

items.title: Care for the elderly must be rotated
items.core: Long-term unilateral commitment is unsustainable.
body: List care tasks.
Convene regular family meetings.
Make a monthly schedule, allocate medical appointments, buy medicines, and stay overnight to your children by week, and give them a reminder one week in advance.
Establish a care log to record blood pressure, medication and diet, and verbally confirm for three minutes before leaving when the shift is over.
In case of sudden hospitalization, a person in charge is designated to coordinate with the hospital, and the others only deliver meals or pay bills according to their division of labor.

Case: Xiao Chen took care of his sick father alone for half a year and was exhausted both physically and mentally. Later, he made an agreement with his brothers and sisters to take care of each of them for a week on a monthly basis. Xiao Chen finally had time to breathe, and the family relationship became more harmonious.

items.title: Medical Decisions Talk Upfront
items.core: No one wants to discuss options during an emergency.
body: Understand the wishes of the elderly.
Specify the contact person.
You can list the elderly’s known diseases, commonly used drugs, and allergic history during physical examination or follow-up consultation, and ask the doctor about common risks.
Clear the wishes for first aid, hospitalization, surgery, intubation, etc. in advance. It is best for the elderly person to express them and write a written memo.
Organize medical insurance, commercial insurance, affordable expenses and contacts into mobile phone memos and present them directly in emergency situations.

Case: Before my father was hospitalized for COPD, the whole family discussed with the doctor at the outpatient clinic whether to intubate, transfer to ICU, and what the cost would be if his condition worsened. Later, when he went to the emergency room, he signed the plan according to the plan without complaining to each other.

items.title: Discuss in advance before making a decision
items.core: Cut first and tell later will hurt trust.
body: Explain the considerations and basis.
Give the other party room to veto.
Setting an amount threshold, such as exceeding a certain percentage of monthly income or unplanned expenses, must be communicated to the co-decision maker first.
Open the discussion with ‘I need to understand your considerations’. Listen to the reasons first, and then explain your concerns and bottom line.
Write clearly the remedial steps for the decision that have occurred, including refunds, stop losses, compensation and how to avoid them in the future.

Case: The husband signed up for a high-priced pension financial management class and paid for it without any discussion. After finding out, the wife asked for a refund and a budget together, and then agreed that expenditures of more than 10,000 yuan should be confirmed at a family meeting.

items.title: When thanking you, be specific
items.core: A general thank you has no memory.
body: tell what the other person did.
Feedback after the results come out.
Tell me what the other party did specifically, for example, ‘You stood in line with me to pay the bill last night and helped me get the checklist.
Explain the results of your help, such as ‘Because you sent the doctor to the doctor in time, my father did not delay in taking the X-ray’.
Reciprocate in a way that is appropriate for the relationship, whether by sending a clear message, buying you a cup of coffee in return, or offering to do a small favor.

Case: A neighbor helped take her mother home from the hospital. Ms. Wang sent a message that night saying thank you for helping her go up and downstairs, talking to her on the way, and gave her fruit the next day. The neighbor said she would still be willing to help in the future.

items.title: Pause in case of conflict
items.core: Anything you say when you are at the peak of your emotions can easily hurt someone.
body: Agreed cooling time.
Return to the question later.
As soon as you raise your voice, interrupt, or bring up old scores, immediately say, "I'll slow down for a moment and continue in twenty minutes."
Do not continue to send messages or block threats when paused. You can make an appointment to return to the desktop at a specific time to avoid being treated coldly.
When resuming the conversation, talk about the facts and needs first, and then choose from the alternatives without evaluating the other party’s character or motives.

Case: A brother and a sister argued over the schedule of accompanying their mother in hospital. The elder brother threw his cell phone on the table, and the younger sister said to stop for twenty minutes. After cooling down, the two rewrote the schedule and softened their tone significantly.

items.title: Review the relationship regularly
items.core: Long-term relationships need to be maintained.
body: Ask each other if they are feeling well lately.
Small problems are solved when they are young.
A fixed frequency, such as once a month or quarterly, choose a time when both parties are not tired, and do not turn the review into a temporary quarrel.
Use three questions: What have been helpful recently, what things have made you tired, and how do you hope to adjust in the next stage.
After the review, one or two executable changes will be formed and written into the family group or calendar. Check the completion status next time.

Case: The couple reviewed the arrangements for taking care of the elderly and housework together on Sunday evenings every quarter. They found that the wife had to work more at night for three consecutive weeks, so they changed to shifts and hired hourly cleaners.

items.title: Ask external help when necessary
items.core: You don’t have to deal with family problems alone.
body: Learn about consultation channels.
If violence occurs, seek help immediately.
First list the types of difficulties, such as care, expenses, emotional or legal risks, and then find the community, hospital, lawyer or psychological consultation accordingly.
Preparing medical history, expense receipts, care records and current problems before asking for help allows outsiders to give advice more quickly.

Agree with your family on the boundaries of external intervention, who will be responsible for contact, who will cooperate with implementation, and what privacy information cannot be disclosed at will.

Case: After the old man became disabled, his daughter quit caring for her for half a year and developed insomnia. She first contacted the community elderly care service station to apply for day care, and then sought psychological counseling. Her sleep improved and there were fewer conflicts with care.

items.title: Protect your home from falls and heat
items.core: Most accidents happen in familiar places.
body: Fixed carpets and cabinet doors.
Keep hot water and knives in a safe place.
Install a night light or sensor light from the bedside to the bathroom, fix the wires along the edges, and press the edges of the carpet with non-slip mats.
Place the hot water kettle, pot handles and freshly cooked utensils out of the reach of children and the elderly, with no vertical lines on the edge of the table.
Ask the elderly to wear non-slip slippers, put handrails and non-slip mats in the bathroom, and use a thermos bottle to get water at night.

Case: The mother went to the kitchen to pour water at night and tripped over the edge of the carpet, resulting in bruises on her knees. The children removed the carpet, installed sensor lights, and moved the hot water bottle to a fixed height, and they did not fall again.

items.title: Regular cleaning of home medicine cabinets
items.core: Expired medicines are more dangerous than myrrh.
body: Organize by category and mark the validity period.
Regularly clean up expired medicines.
Check the medicine box every three months, take out expired, damp, or unclearly labeled medicines separately and recycle them according to regulations.
Label according to ‘name, drug name, dosage, usage, expiration date’, and place commonly used drugs for the elderly where they are easiest to grab.
Distinguish between prescription drugs and spare over-the-counter drugs. Prescription drugs should no longer be taken by others by themselves, and leftover drugs should not be added at will.

Case: When Ms. Li was organizing the medicine box, she found that the antihypertensive medicine was eight months out of date and the labels on the painkillers had fallen off. She repackaged the boxes according to their uses and marked the expiry date to prevent her father from accidentally taking them.

items.title: Chronic diseases of the elderly should be recorded
items.core: Data is more reliable than impressions.
body: Record blood pressure, blood sugar and other indicators.
Bring your records with you when you see a doctor.
Use a notebook or mobile phone form to record blood pressure, blood sugar, heart rate and other indicators, fix the measurement time every day and mark the date.
At the same time, record the name of the drug, dosage, post-administration reactions and abnormalities in diet and exercise, and bring it to the doctor to judge the trend during follow-up visits.
When an obvious abnormality occurs, write down the time of occurrence, how long it lasted, and your actions at the time. Don’t just rely on “I seem to be feeling unwell recently.”

Case: Before the father’s follow-up visit, his daughter recorded her blood pressure, blood sugar, medication time and dizziness on paper for a week. The doctor adjusted the dosage of medicine accordingly, and the number of dizziness decreased after the follow-up visit.

items.title: The whole family knows the emergency contact
items.core: There is no need to find the number temporarily when there is an emergency.
body: Written in a fixed location.
Teach your children how to ask for help.

Write the numbers of first aid, family members, community doctors, real estate agents, and nearby relatives and friends on large-font cards, and stick them next to the phone and on the refrigerator door.
Set emergency contacts and one-touch calling on your mobile phone. Devices used by the elderly should be kept within reach and charged regularly.
Confirm whether the number has changed every quarter, and let the elderly practice ‘who to call and how to say the address’.

Case: The grandmother who lives alone pulled the bathroom call rope after falling in the bathroom. After receiving the reminder, her daughter contacted the emergency department and neighbors. After the door was opened, the ambulance entered the house smoothly.

items.title: Give yourself some alone time
items.core: Caregivers need to be cared for too.
body: Arrange replacement staff in advance.
Do not use exhaustion as a standard.
Fix a period of uninterrupted time every week, even if it is only thirty minutes, write it into the family schedule in advance.
When you are alone, do not do care tasks or check family group messages. You can choose to take a walk, take a bath, listen to music or meet friends.
When caregivers experience persistent insomnia, irritability, or numbness, take the initiative to contact relatives and friends or seek professional support.

Case: Xiao Chen took care of his mother with dementia and did not go out for three months. Later, he left his mother with his sister for two hours every Wednesday afternoon and went for a walk by himself. The number of emotional breakdowns was significantly reduced.

items.title: Be anti-slip in your home
items.core: Bathrooms and kitchens are high-risk areas.
body: Place anti-slip mat.
Keep the ground dry.
Cover the bathroom floor with non-slip mats and clean them regularly. Wipe the bathroom in time after bathing. Place absorbent slippers or floor mats at the door.
Install firm handrails next to the toilet and in the shower area. Do not use towel racks as handrails. The bolts must be checked regularly.
Wipe up any oil or water on the kitchen floor immediately, lay anti-slip mats in front of the stove, and try to wear heeled, non-slip shoes for the elderly.

Case: When my mother-in-law came out of the bathroom after taking a bath, her feet slipped and she held on to the door frame. The children laid out non-slip mats, installed handrails, and fixed the shower gel bottle on the wall that day, and it stopped slipping again.

items.title: Kitchen Knives and Fire Management
items.core: Children are curious but lack judgment.
body: Knives should be locked or placed high.
Keep children away while cooking.
Keep knives, lighters and flammable objects away from the stove, and allow children to exit the kitchen or stand outside the safety line when cooking.
Immediately put the knives back into the high drawer after use and lock them, and place the pot handles inward to prevent children from reaching or knocking them over.
If you must leave while cooking, turn off the heat and take away the spatula; teach your children not to touch switches or play with matches.

Case: My mother answered the phone while cooking at night and left the spatula on the gas stove. The five-year-old child stood on tiptoe to touch the knife rest. She immediately turned off the heat, put the knives away in a lockable drawer, and asked the child to retreat to the living room to avoid burns and cuts.

items.title: Pharmaceuticals and detergents locked
items.core: The risk of accidental ingestion is often underestimated.
body: Keep original packaging.
Do not put in food containers.
Put medicines and detergents in a locked cabinet immediately after purchase. Do not use child-proof bottles as your only protection.
The medicine box should retain its original packaging and instructions, and mark the opening date. Expired medicines should be bagged separately and discarded promptly.
Explain to children that medicine is different from candy. Medicines in visitor bags should also be kept handy to avoid accidental taking and eating out of curiosity.

Case: Grandma put cold medicine on the coffee table over the weekend, and the child ate two pieces as candy, and then suffered abdominal pain and vomiting. The family immediately took the medicine box to the doctor. The doctor processed it according to its ingredients and reminded that medicines and cleaning agents at home must be locked up.

items.title: Carry out home escape drills
items.core: You won’t panic if you know the route.
body: Agreed meeting point.
Practice every six months.
Fire and earthquake evacuation drills are conducted every six months, and two meeting points are fixed so that each family member can tell the route.
During the drill, close the electric gate and gas valve, do not take the elevator, and focus on practicing low-profile evacuation and gathering at the door.
After the drill, record the time and stuck points, and adjust the division of labor at the door, night lighting, and support for the elderly.

Case: There was a power outage in the community at night, accompanied by the smell of smoke in the corridor. The father followed the rehearsal route and took the children to bend down and take the stairs along the wall. The mother turned off the gas and took the certificate. The whole family arrived at the meeting point downstairs in three minutes.

items.title: Measures to prevent lost children
items.core: It is easy to get distracted in crowded places.
body: Write contact information for your children.
Promise to stand where you are when you can’t find it.
Wear clothes with eye-catching colors for your children before going out, put parent phone cards in their pockets, and wear contact bracelets for younger children.
When you go to a shopping mall or station, agree on a meeting point first, and tell your children to find a uniformed person or the service desk if they get separated.
Take a photo of what you are wearing that day and agree not to leave with strangers and not to tell strangers your address and mobile phone number.

Case: While visiting a shopping mall during the National Day, the child was crowded out by the crowd in the toy area. The mother put a contact number bracelet on him in advance, and the child asked the service desk to report the number. The parents arrived to pick him up ten minutes later.

items.title: Pay attention to your children’s online safety
items.core: Online risks are just as real.
body: Understand the platform you are using.
Personal information will not be disclosed.
Enable youth mode and privacy permissions for your children, and regularly check your friend list, chat history, and download apps.
We agreed not to click on unfamiliar links, not to scan QR codes from unknown sources, and not to send verification codes or home addresses to netizens.
Use different passwords for the account and bind the parent-manageable email address to enable two-step verification and payment limit reminders.

Case: Xiaoyu, a first-year junior high school student, received a free skin link in a game group, and after filling in his mobile phone number and verification code, his account was stolen. The father discovered the abnormal login and immediately changed his password, froze the payment and contacted the platform to retrieve it.

items.title: Remind the elderly to prevent fraud
items.core: The elderly are a high-frequency victim group.
body: Explain common routines.
Discuss before committing to large expenditures.
Make an agreement with the elderly that if transfers, verification codes, and bank card passwords are involved, hang up the phone first and then confirm with family members.
Help the elderly to enable caller recognition on their mobile phones, delete unfamiliar investment groups, and save bank and public security numbers in quick dials.
Tell us about a scam every month with a real case, and remind you to verify whether you receive a prize for free, recycle it at a high price, or borrow money from acquaintances.

Case: My neighbor Uncle Zhang received a call for social security reissue, and the other party asked to transfer the handling fee first. He hung up first and went to the community to ask the staff. He found out that it was a scam and saved 20,000 yuan in pension money.

items.title: Chronic disease indicators need to be recorded
items.core: The data is more reliable than memory.
body: Measurement based on fixed time.
Bring your records with you when you see a doctor.
Measure blood pressure, blood sugar or heart rate at the same time every day, and record the value, date, medication and abnormal symptoms.
Use paper forms or mobile phone memos to record continuously, instead of just relying on memory, it can be used by doctors to judge trends during follow-up visits.
Set the abnormal threshold. If it exceeds the range, retest quietly first. If the abnormality is still abnormal, contact the doctor in time and save the record.

Case: Aunt Li, who has high blood pressure, gets up early every day to measure her blood pressure and record it. She will take out a two-month form during follow-up visits. The doctor found that the number was higher at night, and after adjusting the medication time, the number of dizziness was significantly reduced.

items.title: Insurance documents are stored in a centralized place
items.core: and can be found when needed.
body: Save photos in the cloud.
Inform family members of location.
Use a waterproof document bag to store insurance policies, payment vouchers, invoices and claims telephone numbers, with the insurance type written on the cover.
Take a screenshot of the electronic policy and back it up to the cloud disk, print a copy for your family files, and mark the policy number and effective date.
Check the beneficiary, payment status and coverage every six months, and update the contact and information immediately after changes.

Case: When my father was hospitalized and needed reimbursement, my family rummaged through the drawers and couldn't find the insurance policy. Later, I found a printed copy of the electronic policy in the document bag, submitted the materials according to the list, and the reimbursement was received in two weeks.

items.title: 准备备用电源
items.core: 保证通讯设备可用。
body: Charge the power bank regularly.
Place it in a fixed location.
Prepare a power bank and a short charging cable with sufficient capacity, check the power every month, and charge it fully before power outage.
Enable power-saving mode on your mobile phone and keep family, property, hospital and power supply repair phone numbers as quick contacts.
Store spare batteries according to the instructions, avoid high temperature and moisture, and check them every quarter if not used for a long time.

Case: There was a power outage in the community on the night of a typhoon. Mr. Wang used a power bank that had been filled in advance to power his mobile phone and router. He kept in touch with his family and received a property restoration notice before dawn.

items.title: Build mutual aid with neighbors
items.core: Neighbors are the fastest in times of emergency.
body: Get to know people who live on the same floor.
Leave your contact information.
Exchange phone numbers, WeChat messages, and emergency contacts with neighboring residents to explain the conditions of the elderly, children, or patients at home.
We agree to pay attention to each other when we go out. If there are piles at the door for a long time or the lights are not on for a long time, we can call to inquire.
Share a small amount of emergency supplies information, such as fire extinguishers, first aid kits, and tool boxes, so that you can quickly borrow them in an emergency.

Case: An old man living alone fell down in the kitchen at night, holding on to the wall and knocking on the door next door. When the young man heard about it, he came to her home. He first contacted her family members and then accompanied her to the emergency room. They exchanged phone calls at ordinary times so that the rescue could not be delayed.

items.title: Do regular home safety inspections
items.core: Hidden dangers will appear as life changes.
body: Go through the list item by item.
Deal with the problem immediately if you find it.
Check the expiry dates of smoke detectors, gas alarms, and fire extinguishers every quarter, and replace or recharge them immediately if they become invalid.
Check whether the wires are aging, whether the plug strips are overloaded, and whether the sockets are loose. If problems are found, stop using them before repairing them.
Adjust the inspection focus with the seasons, check for water leaks in rainy season, check heating equipment in winter, and review the guardrails as the children grow up.

Case: Three months after moving into the new home, my father checked according to the checklist and found that the balcony power strip was old and the bathroom floor was slippery. He replaced the power strip and laid a non-slip mat, so the child never slipped again after taking a bath.

items.title: Centralized management of important documents
items.core: Scattered storage is easy to miss.
body: Use fireproof and moisture-proof boxes.
Inform trusted family members of their location.
Put your ID card, household register, passport, birth certificate, and real estate certificate into a labeled file box and store it in a fixed location.
Copies and electronic scans of certificates are backed up separately, and copies are carried with you for external offices. Try not to borrow originals at will.
Return it to its place immediately after each use, designate two people to know the storage location, clean up expired certificates promptly and remind them to replace them.

Case: On the day of child registration, parents discovered that the household register and birth certificate were in two places and almost missed submitting them. After that, they used labeled file boxes to collect the documents, and successfully handed in all the materials on the same day when applying for transfer.
